- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish or sideways bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is positive — cap forecast rise to 5-7% above recent peak.
- In mean-reversion scenarios (sentiment oscillating), model often fails to correct quickly — adjust forecast to converge toward 3-5 day moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates upward trends in early forecast window (first 7-10 days) when sentiment is bullish — add 1-2% buffer to early forecast values.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast using 5-day rolling average or reduce volatility penalty in optimization.
